papers.title: DiffMethylTools: a toolbox for the detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic mechanism, and its significant changes (i.e., differential methylation) regulate gene expression, cell-type specification, and disease progression without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Differential methylation has traditionally been detected by statistical comparison of two groups using existing tools and has supported a wide range of downstream analyses in human disease studies. However, few toolboxes efficiently integrate robust detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation, and the reproducibility of detected signals
papers.summary: DiffMethylTools is a new toolbox that integrates detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation in a single, user-friendly framework. It aims to improve efficiency and reproducibility compared to existing tools, which often lack integrated downstream analysis features.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation Reveal that METTL9 Drives Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression via TGF-β/Smad-Mediated EMT Activation.
papers.abstract: Methyltransferase-like 9 (METTL9) has been implicated in tumor progression, yet its clinical significance, functional roles, and immunoregulatory functions in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear. This study aimed to integrate multi-omics datasets and experimental evidence to systematically evaluate the expression profile, prognostic value, molecular mechanisms, and tumor microenvironment (TME)-related functions of METTL9 in LUAD.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to show that METTL9 is upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma and drives tumor progression by activating TGF-β/Smad-mediated epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The findings suggest METTL9 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.title: WebCVTree4: Phylogenetic and Taxonomic Study Platform for Prokaryotes base on Whole Genomes.
papers.abstract: CVTree is an alignment-free methodology for inferring species phylogeny and taxonomy. This method allows for the efficient and accurate resolution of evolutionary relationships among large numbers of species based on whole-genome sequencing data. Since 2004, we have been continuously providing CVTree web services. Recently, the server has undergone a significant upgrade, culminating in the release of the WebCVTree4 platform. This upgrade involves a comprehensive update of the built-in genomic database. The core algorithm has been optimized to enable online phylogenetic reconstruction for tens
papers.summary: WebCVTree4 is an upgraded web platform for alignment-free phylogenetic and taxonomic analysis of prokaryotes using whole-genome data. It features an updated genomic database and optimized algorithms for efficient online tree reconstruction, supporting evolutionary studies of large species sets.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling enables subclassification of mucinous ovarian carcinoma and distinguishes it from extraovarian mucinous metastases.
papers.abstract: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) is an epithelial ovarian cancer subtype that is frequently misclassified as extraovarian mucinous metastasis (EOM) because of overlapping features. To address this diagnostic challenge, we perform genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of 58 MOCs, 38 EOMs, and 18 mucinous borderline ovarian tumors (mBOTs) collected from six institutions. Methylation analysis defines two mBOT groups, one epigenetically similar to normal ovary and one resembling MOC. Unsupervised clustering reveals two distinct MOC methylation subtypes with potential prognostic relevance in the in
papers.summary: This study uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling to distinguish mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) from extraovarian mucinous metastases (EOM), which are often misdiagnosed due to overlapping features. The analysis identifies distinct methylation subtypes of MOC with potential prognostic relevance, offering a new diagnostic tool to improve classification and patient management.

papers.title: Protocol for detecting causal variants by co-localizing GWAS and QTL studies using colocRedRibbon.
papers.abstract: Here, we present a protocol for using colocRedRibbon to link disease-associated variants to gene expression variation by co-localizing genome-wide association study (GWAS) SNPs with cis-expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs). We describe steps for shortlisting GWAS and eQTL variants, computing co-localization statistics, and assessing posterior probabilities. Co-localized variants provide insights into disease mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets. Beyond GWAS-eQTL integration, the protocol can be applied to co-localization analyses across different QTL types and distinct GWAS datas
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes how to use colocRedRibbon to identify causal variants by co-localizing GWAS signals with eQTLs, linking disease-associated SNPs to gene expression changes. It provides step-by-step instructions for variant selection, co-localization analysis, and interpretation of posterior probabilities, with applicability beyond eQTLs to other QTL types and GWAS datasets.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging field of spatial biology in cancer epigenetics, highlighting how spatial transcriptomics and related technologies are being used to study epigenetic regulation within the context of tissue architecture. It emphasizes the importance of capturing spatial context to understand tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions, and points to future directions for integrating epigenomic information with spatial data.

papers.title: ALPAR: Automated Learning Pipeline for Antimicrobial Resistance.
papers.abstract: The field of machine learning in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) research has experienced rapid growth, fueled by advancements in high-throughput genome sequencing and the growing capacity of computational resources. However, the complexity and lack of standardized data preparation and bioinformatic analyses present significant challenges, especially for newcomers to the domain. In response to these challenges, we introduce ALPAR (Automated Learning Pipeline for Antimicrobial Resistance), a comprehensive AMR data analysis tool covering the entire process from processing of raw genomic data to t
papers.summary: ALPAR is a new automated pipeline that simplifies antimicrobial resistance (AMR) analysis by handling everything from raw genomic data processing to machine learning model training, making it accessible to researchers new to the field. It addresses the lack of standardized workflows in AMR bioinformatics by providing a comprehensive, end-to-end tool.

papers.title: Identification of Potential Biomarkers for Rheumatoid Arthritis Based on Integrated Bioinformatics and Single-Cell RNA-Seq.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that causes progressive joint damage and systemic complications. Despite multiple treatment options, many patients fail to achieve sustained remission. Our study aimed to integrate bioinformatics and single-cell RNA-seq analyses to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets and explore bioactive compounds from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM).
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for rheumatoid arthritis, and explores traditional Chinese medicine compounds that may target them. The findings offer candidate genes and drug leads that could inform future diagnostic and treatment strategies for RA.

papers.title: Evaluating Somatic Mutational Contamination in Large-Scale Germline Genomic Studies.
papers.abstract: Large-scale genomic initiatives like the UK Biobank have revolutionized our understanding of human disease. These studies typically assume that blood-derived DNA faithfully reflects an individual's germline genome. However, this assumption is challenged by somatic mutations arising from processes like clonal hematopoiesis. Although standard bioinformatics pipelines employ variant allele frequency (VAF)-based filtering to mitigate such contamination, the efficacy of these approaches requires systematic evaluation. By systematically analyzing germline genome data from large cohorts through appli
papers.summary: This paper evaluates how somatic mutations, particularly from clonal hematopoiesis, can contaminate germline genomic data in large-scale studies like the UK Biobank. The authors systematically assess the effectiveness of standard VAF-based filtering methods and highlight potential limitations, suggesting that contamination may persist and impact downstream analyses.

papers.title: A De Novo Algorithm for Allele Reconstruction from Oxford Nanopore Amplicon Reads, with Application to CYP2D6.
papers.abstract: The Oxford Nanopore Technologies' sequencing platform offers a path towards bedside genomics, producing long reads that can completely cover a gene of interest, and detect any known or novel variant the gene contains. However, the analysis of these long reads to identify actionable genotypes remains challenging and typically requires customization depending on the target gene.
papers.summary: This paper presents a new de novo algorithm for reconstructing alleles from Oxford Nanopore amplicon sequencing data, specifically applied to the pharmacogene CYP2D6. The method aims to simplify and streamline the analysis of long reads to identify actionable genotypes without extensive gene-specific customization.

papers.title: Exploring the use of machine and deep learning in genome-wide association studies: a comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: The advent of high-throughput sequencing technologies has generated increasingly large and complex genomic datasets, necessitating analytical approaches capable of capturing high-dimensional and potentially nonlinear genetic interactions. This situation has significantly impacted the entire field of Genome-Wide Association Study (GWAS), whose primary goal is the identification of genomic traits and variants that are statistically associated with the risk of a disease. However, traditional GWAS methods may show reduced performance when applied to highly polygenic and nonlinear genetic architect
papers.summary: This comprehensive review examines the application of machine and deep learning methods to genome-wide association studies (GWAS), highlighting their potential to capture complex, nonlinear genetic interactions that traditional approaches may miss. It discusses the challenges and opportunities of these advanced analytical techniques for identifying disease-associated genomic variants in increasingly large and high-dimensional datasets.

papers.title: Impact of M and E protein mutations in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants on reduced antibody binding and increased structural stability: a bioinformatics study (2021-2023).
papers.abstract: First identified in late 2021, the Omicron variant of SARS-CoV-2 accumulated substantially more mutations than previously circulating variants. This study investigated the genomic characteristics and structural consequences of mutations in the membrane (M) and envelope (E) proteins of dominant Omicron lineages circulating in southern Iran between March 2021 and March 2023.
papers.summary: This study analyzed mutations in the membrane (M) and envelope (E) proteins of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants from southern Iran, finding that specific mutations reduce antibody binding while increasing structural stability. The findings suggest these mutations may contribute to immune escape and enhanced viral fitness.

papers.title: Discovery of a DNA methylation episignature for Weiss-Kruszka syndrome.
papers.abstract: Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WSKA; OMIM 618619) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of ZNF462, a zinc-finger transcription factor involved in chromatin regulation and early embryonic development. WSKA is characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia, craniofacial dysmorphic features (around 8) and variable congenital anomalies. Genome-wide DNAm profiling was performed on peripheral blood DNA from 9 WSKA cases with (likely) pathogenic ZNF462 variants and matched controls to look for differential methylation. Analysis using the EpiSign™ pipeline ide
papers.summary: This study identifies a distinct DNA methylation episignature for Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WSKA), a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by ZNF462 mutations. Using genome-wide DNA methylation profiling on blood samples from affected individuals, the authors found a specific methylation pattern that could serve as a diagnostic biomarker for WSKA.

papers.title: First molecular detection of the genus Almendravirus in Johnbelkinia ulopus and Anopheles apicimacula mosquitoes from the Colombian Caribbean.
papers.abstract: Rhabdoviridae includes many viruses, among which rabies virus is notable. Other genera in this family can infect mammals, birds, reptiles, fish, and plants.
papers.summary: This study reports the first molecular detection of Almendravirus, a genus within the Rhabdoviridae family, in two mosquito species (Johnbelkinia ulopus and Anopheles apicimacula) collected from the Colombian Caribbean. The finding expands the known geographic range and host range of this understudied virus genus, which may have implications for understanding arbovirus ecology and evolution.

papers.title: Rare variant analysis of whole genome sequenced juvenile idiopathic arthritis multiplex pedigrees identifies rare variants in NOD2 and ACVR1.
papers.abstract: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is a complex rheumatic disease that is influenced by environmental and genetic factors. Linkage studies and genome-wide association studies have identified genes that contribute to the risk of developing JIA but are limited in their ability to identify disease-risk variants of large effect. Penetrant, heritable risk variants can be detected in high-risk families, but such cases are uncommon due to the low prevalence of JIA. This study utilizes whole-genome sequencing of 23 multiplex families, the largest such cohort to date, to discover variants and genes re
papers.summary: This study used whole-genome sequencing of 23 multiplex families with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), the largest cohort of its kind, to identify rare variants associated with disease risk. They found rare variants in NOD2 and ACVR1 genes, suggesting these may contribute to JIA susceptibility in high-risk families.

papers.title: RNA and Mitochondrial Reprogramming Associated with Azacytidine Treatment in Higher-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Aims: Treatment of higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (HR-MDS) with azacytidine (AZA) exerts significant effects on the epigenome, primarily through DNA demethylation and reactivation of epigenetically silenced genes. Beyond this established mechanism, molecular AZA-linked effects are increasingly being recognized. Materials and methods: Liquid chromatography combined with mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) was employed for the accurate assessment of various RNA and DNA modifications pre- and post-AZA treatment of an HR-MDS cohort (N = 8). Mapping of the AZA treatment-responsive regulatory pathwa
papers.summary: This pilot study investigates the effects of azacytidine (AZA) treatment on RNA and mitochondrial reprogramming in higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (HR-MDS). Using LC-MS/MS, the authors measured RNA and DNA modifications before and after AZA treatment in a small cohort, revealing treatment-responsive regulatory pathways beyond DNA demethylation.

papers.title: Natural compounds as epigenetic modulators in gynaecological cancers: From chemoresistance to precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Gynaecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial malignancies, remain major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality because of tumour heterogeneity, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance. Epigenetic dysregulation, involving aberrant DNA methylation, altered histone modifications, dysregulated non-coding RNAs, and N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) RNA remodelling, contributes to these processes. Direct evidence that natural compounds modulate m⁶A machinery in gynaecological cancers remains absent and is considered a knowledge gap.
papers.summary: This review examines how natural compounds can modulate epigenetic mechanisms—such as DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs—in gynaecological cancers, with a focus on overcoming chemoresistance and advancing precision oncology. It identifies a knowledge gap regarding the direct modulation of m6A RNA modifications by these compounds in this cancer context.

papers.title: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in Drosophila eugracilis.
papers.abstract: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in the D. eugracilis Apr. 2013 (BCM-HGSC/Deug_2.0) (DeugGB2) Genome Assembly (GenBank Accession: GCA_000236325.2) of Drosophila eugracilis. This ortholog was characterized as part of a developing dataset to study the evolution of the Insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway (IIS) across the genus Drosophila using the Genomics Education Partnership gene annotation protocol for Course-based Undergraduate Research Experiences.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a gene model for the raptor ortholog in Drosophila eugracilis, annotated as part of a course-based undergraduate research project studying the evolution of the insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway across Drosophila species. The work provides a specific genomic annotation resource for this species.

papers.title: Using Deep Learning Models of Gene Regulation to Guide Drug Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Background: Drug repurposing offers a cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic discovery, but most computational approaches do not model noncoding genetic variation. Because over 90% of genome-wide association study (GWAS) risk variants reside in noncoding regions, linking regulatory variation to therapeutic hypotheses remains a major challenge. Methods: We developed an integrative deep learning framework that links allele-specific enhancer prediction to candidate therapeutics through two complementary prioritization strategies, a transcription factor (TF)-based and a gene-based appro
papers.summary: This paper presents an integrative deep learning framework that uses allele-specific enhancer predictions from noncoding GWAS variants to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. The approach links regulatory variation to therapeutics via transcription factor- and gene-based strategies, addressing the challenge that most risk variants lie in noncoding regions.

papers.title: SorghumHub: featuring the next phase for the KBCommons web portal with new molecular biology features.
papers.abstract: Genomic resources for underutilized crops like sorghum [Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] often lag behind major staples, hindering efforts to link genetic diversity to agronomic traits. Improvements in genomic sequencing and bioinformatics have advanced crop genomics, yet species-specific challenges persist in the lack of tailored genomic resources, limiting precision breeding and applied genomics applications.
papers.summary: SorghumHub is a new web portal that provides enhanced genomic resources and molecular biology features for sorghum, an underutilized crop. It aims to bridge the gap in genomic tools for sorghum, facilitating the link between genetic diversity and agronomic traits for precision breeding.

papers.title: PG2: algorithms and a web-based tool for effective layout and visual analysis of pangenome graphs.
papers.abstract: The advent of cost-effective whole-genome assembly has enabled the creation of comprehensive pangenomes with resolved haplotypes across various organisms. This technological leap drives the refinement of tailored methodologies to manage the intricate sequences and variations in extensive collections of related genomes. These methodologies often utilize graphical representations of pangenomes to enhance algorithms for tasks like sequence alignment, visualization, and functional genomics. Leveraging the insights provided by pangenomes, these approaches exhibit improved efficiency in bioinformati
papers.summary: This paper introduces PG2, a new algorithm and web-based tool designed to improve the layout and visual analysis of pangenome graphs. It addresses the challenge of effectively visualizing complex genomic variation across multiple related genomes, offering a practical resource for researchers working with pangenome data.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing of single cell-derived melanoma sublines reveals divergent and parallel genomic and epigenomic evolutionary trajectories.
papers.abstract: Tumor evolution is driven by various mutational processes, ranging from single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) to large structural variants (SVs) to dynamic shifts in DNA methylation. Current short-read sequencing methods struggle to accurately capture the full spectrum of these genomic and epigenomic alterations due to inherent technical limitations. To overcome that, here we introduce an approach to identify and analyze the genomic and epigenetic events in different stages of tumoral evolution from long-read sequencing of single-cell derived sublines. We then use it to profile 23 sublines of a mo
papers.summary: This study introduces a long-read sequencing approach to analyze genomic and epigenomic evolution in single-cell-derived melanoma sublines, capturing SNVs, structural variants, and DNA methylation changes that short-read methods miss. Profiling 23 sublines reveals both divergent and parallel evolutionary trajectories, highlighting the power of long-read sequencing for comprehensive tumor evolution analysis.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) to identify epigenetic regulators essential for pluripotency in mouse embryonic stem cells, revealing an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the transition between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: ROS-Centered Transcriptomic Regulatory Networks Linking Salinity Stress, Antioxidant Defense and Processability Traits in Salicornia spp.
papers.abstract: Salinity stress affects not only the survival and productivity of halophytic plants, but also the composition, structure and processability of their biomass. In Salicornia spp., salt-induced regulation of ion transport, osmotic adjustment, reactive oxygen species signaling, antioxidant defense, and cell wall remodeling can directly influence residual salinity, water retention, texture, extractability, drying behavior, and oxidative stability of plant biomass. However, most existing transcriptomic studies of Salicornia and related halophytes have focused mainly on salt tolerance mechanisms, whe
papers.summary: This study investigates how salinity stress shapes transcriptomic regulatory networks in Salicornia spp., linking reactive oxygen species signaling, antioxidant defense, and cell wall remodeling to biomass processability traits such as water retention, texture, and drying behavior. It highlights that salt-induced gene expression changes not only support halophyte survival but also directly influence the industrial quality of the plant material.

papers.title: Circulating Tumor DNA as a Biomarker of Treatment Response and Minimal Residual Disease in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common subtype of aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma and is characterized by pronounced molecular heterogeneity that is not always fully captured by standard histopathological assessment. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is increasingly regarded as a promising liquid-biopsy biomarker that enables non-invasive molecular tumor profiling, assessment of tumor burden, dynamic monitoring of treatment response, and detection of measurable/minimal residual disease (MRD). Modern analytical platforms, ranging from PCR-based assays to next-generation sequencing
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) as a non-invasive liquid biopsy biomarker for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), highlighting its role in molecular profiling, tumor burden assessment, treatment response monitoring, and detection of minimal residual disease. It covers various analytical platforms, from PCR to next-generation sequencing, and underscores the potential of ctDNA to complement standard histopathology in managing this heterogeneous cancer.

papers.title: MORF4L1, encoding a chromatin remodeler, is mutated in a recognizable dysmorphic neurodevelopmental disorder.
papers.abstract: Chromatin remodelers are increasingly recognized as key contributors to neurodevelopmental disorders, usually through de novo dominant variants. Mortality Factor 4 Like 1 (MORF4L1) is recognized for its role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation. We identified a consanguineous Middle Eastern family in which a neurodevelopmental disorder with a distinctive dysmorphic phenotype segregated with a homozygous variant in MORF4L1.  The autosomal recessive inheritance sets it apart from most other chromatin remodeling disorders. Consistent with its epigenetic role, we also observed
papers.summary: This study identifies a homozygous variant in MORF4L1, a chromatin remodeler, as the cause of a distinctive neurodevelopmental disorder with dysmorphic features in a consanguineous family. The autosomal recessive inheritance pattern is unusual for chromatin remodeling disorders, which are typically dominant. The findings expand the genetic spectrum of chromatin-related neurodevelopmental conditions.

papers.title: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in Drosophila erecta.
papers.abstract: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in the May 2011 (Agencourt Dere_CAF1/DereCAF1) Genome Assembly (GenBank Accession: GCA_000005135.1) of Drosophila erecta. This ortholog was characterized as part of a developing dataset to study the evolution of the Insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway (IIS) across the genus Drosophila using the Genomics Education Partnership gene annotation protocol for Course-based Undergraduate Research Experiences.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a gene model for the raptor ortholog in Drosophila erecta, annotated as part of a course-based undergraduate research effort to study the evolution of the insulin/IGF signaling pathway across Drosophila species. The work provides a genomic annotation resource for this species, contributing to comparative evolutionary studies.

papers.title: amR: an R package suite to predict antimicrobial resistance in bacterial pathogens.
papers.abstract: Identifying bacterial antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is critical for diagnostics and treatment, but resistance is a complex trait arising from myriad mechanisms spanning multiple molecular scales. Existing computational approaches often function as black boxes and rarely explore cross-species or multi-drug patterns. We developed amR, an integrated R package suite that provides a complete framework from bacterial genome data curation to interpretable AMR predictions, enabling identification of resistance mechanisms across species and drugs.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: amR is a new R package suite that provides an integrated framework for predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacteria, from genome data curation to interpretable predictions. It addresses limitations of existing black-box tools by enabling cross-species and multi-drug analysis, helping identify resistance mechanisms across different bacterial species and drugs.

papers.title: A Pan-Methylome Framework for Population-Scale Bacterial Epigenomics.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic modifications furnish a hidden regulatory layer that shapes cellular fate and evolutionary potential without rewriting the genetic code. In eukaryotes, methylome maps have profoundly transformed our understanding of development, disease, and lineage diversification. In bacteria, which represent the most abundant and ecologically versatile forms of life, the epigenome remains a largely uncharted dimension. To enable population-scale comparison of bacterial methylomes, we develop a principled strategy to prioritize methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded, broadly conserved
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new framework for comparing bacterial methylomes at population scale, focusing on methylation systems that are enzymatically encoded and broadly conserved. It provides a principled strategy to prioritize these systems, enabling large-scale epigenetic analysis in bacteria, an area that has been largely unexplored compared to eukaryotes.

papers.title: Construction and Evaluation of a High-Quality Reference Panel for Dairy Goats.
papers.abstract: High-quality reference panels are important resources for genotype imputation and genomic selection in dairy goats; however, dairy-goat reference panels remain limited in sample size, population representation, and standardized workflow evaluation. In this study, 1092 dairy-goat samples from multiple populations, and public resequencing datasets, were integrated to construct and evaluate a dairy-goat reference panel for low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (lcWGS) and SNP-array data. Phasing and imputation strategies were compared using Beagle 5.4, SHAPEIT5, GLIMPSE2, and a BaseVar + Beagle pi
papers.summary: This study constructs a high-quality reference panel for dairy goats by integrating 1,092 samples from multiple populations and public resequencing data, and evaluates different phasing and imputation strategies for low-coverage whole-genome sequencing and SNP-array data. The work addresses the need for more comprehensive and standardized reference panels in dairy goat genomics, which are essential for accurate genotype imputation and genomic selection.

papers.title: T-DNA Analyzer: A Long-Read Sequencing Pipeline for Characterizing T-DNA Insertion Sites in Transgenic Crops.
papers.abstract: Molecular characterization of the transferred DNA (T-DNA) insertion sites is required for the safety assessment of genetically modified (GM) crops, yet conventional PCR-based methods are labor-intensive and limited in their ability to resolve complex structural variations. We present T-DNA Analyzer, an integrated bioinformatics pipeline that transforms long-read sequencing data (PacBio HiFi or Oxford Nanopore) into a comprehensive insertion site report. The pipeline implements a host-derived read filter that subtracts host-homologous vector regions to eliminate false-positive chimeric read cal
papers.summary: T-DNA Analyzer is a new bioinformatics pipeline that uses long-read sequencing data (PacBio HiFi or Oxford Nanopore) to comprehensively characterize T-DNA insertion sites in transgenic crops, overcoming the limitations of traditional PCR-based methods. It includes a host-derived read filter to reduce false positives and generates detailed insertion site reports, which could streamline the safety assessment of genetically modified crops.

papers.title: Integrating epigenetic and metabolic indicators for non-invasive endometrial cancer triage: a machine learning approach.
papers.abstract: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is a primary symptom indicative of endometrial cancer (EC), yet its diagnosis still primarily relies on invasive biopsy. This study aimed to develop and validate a non-invasive, interpretable machine learning (ML) model integrating local epigenetic (exfoliated cell CDO1 methylation) and systemic metabolic indicators for EC triage.
papers.summary: This study developed a non-invasive machine learning model that combines local epigenetic markers (CDO1 methylation in exfoliated cells) with systemic metabolic indicators to triage patients with abnormal uterine bleeding for endometrial cancer, potentially reducing the need for invasive biopsies. The model is interpretable and aims to improve diagnostic accuracy in a clinical setting.

papers.title: Safeguarding open-weight genomic foundation models through weight locking.
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models can dramatically accelerate biological research by learning general-purpose representations of genomic data that transfer across tasks, enabling researchers to predict variant effects, regulatory elements, and molecular function, among others. To safeguard against potential biosecurity threats and malicious misuse of open-weight models, a common strategy involves excluding human-infecting viral genomes from the model's training corpora. This strategy, however, can be easily circumvented by fine-tuning models on abundantly available viral data. Weight-locking with spec
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint proposes 'weight locking' as a safeguard for open-weight genomic foundation models, preventing fine-tuning on excluded viral data that could enable biosecurity threats. The method aims to block malicious adaptation while preserving the model's utility for legitimate research tasks.

papers.title: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling: Technologies, computation, and applications in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Cancer is an intrinsically heterogeneous disease characterized by distinct malignant subclones defined by specific genetic and epigenetic alterations, such as aberrant DNA methylation. Traditional bulk sequencing methods analyze large populations of cells in aggregate, yielding an averaged methylome signal that masks the rare but clinically significant epigenetic patterns driving tumor initiation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. The emergence of single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAme) sequencing has driven a paradigm shift in oncology by providing the resolution required to dissect this
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell DNA methylation sequencing technologies are transforming precision oncology by revealing epigenetic heterogeneity that bulk sequencing masks. It covers the technical and computational advances in the field and their applications in understanding tumor evolution, metastasis, and drug resistance.

papers.title: A generator-matrix causal-inference framework separates measurable aging biomarkers from mortality-driving latent dynamics in humans.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in computational geroscience is to distinguish molecular quantities that predict mortality from those that causally drive it. Epigenetic clocks and aging biomarkers are increasingly used as if they were that mechanism, yet this is rarely tested directly. This distinction also bears on competing theories of aging: damage/reliability (A), hyperfunction/mTOR-IIS (B-1), and information loss (B-2). Although individual aging proteins have been tested piecemeal, no study has asked, in one framework, what fraction of mortality is measurable, whether it is causal, and whether it is
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a generator-matrix causal-inference framework to separate biomarkers that merely predict mortality from latent dynamics that causally drive it, applied to human aging data. The framework tests competing aging theories and quantifies the causal fraction of mortality, offering a new way to interpret epigenetic clocks and aging biomarkers.

papers.title: Integrating multi-ancestry common and rare variant mapping accelerates therapeutic target discovery.
papers.abstract: Integrating human genetics into therapeutic discovery accelerates drug development. However, ancestral biases in historical cohorts have left critical functional variation largely uncharted. Here, we leverage the diverse NIH All of Us Research Program to conduct comprehensive common- and rare-variant association analyses for 624 quantitative traits across 369,655 ancestrally diverse individuals. We identified 6,181 genome-wide significant locus-trait associations (526 novel) and 416 gene-trait associations (105 novel) via rare-variant burden testing. By integrating fine-mapping with computatio
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint reports a large-scale multi-ancestry genetic association study using the NIH All of Us Research Program, analyzing 624 quantitative traits in nearly 370,000 diverse individuals. The authors identified thousands of novel common and rare variant associations, and integrated fine-mapping with computational methods to prioritize therapeutic targets, demonstrating the value of diverse cohorts for drug discovery.

papers.title: TNEAtlas: A Pan-cancer Database to Identify and Characterize Transcribed Non-coding Elements.
papers.abstract: Advances in precision oncology have underscored the need to move beyond regulatory frameworks centered on protein-coding regions and better understand regulatory mechanisms within the non-coding genome. To systematically characterize transcribed non-coding elements (TNEs) in cancer, we developed an automated computational framework that integrates 130 RNA-seq datasets from 26 cancer types and 16 human tissues and identifies more than 2 million intergenic TNEs. In parallel, we established the first pan-cancer TNE database, TNEAtlas, which annotates TNEs with epigenetic signatures and functional
papers.summary: The authors developed TNEAtlas, a comprehensive pan-cancer database that identifies and characterizes over 2 million transcribed non-coding elements (TNEs) by integrating 130 RNA-seq datasets from 26 cancer types and 16 tissues. This resource provides epigenetic annotations and functional insights, moving beyond protein-coding regions to better understand regulatory mechanisms in the non-coding genome.

papers.title: Comprehensive epigenetic landscape of Sulfur Mustard (SM) exposure in HaCaT keratinocytes.
papers.abstract: Sulfur Mustard (SM) is a potent vesicant chemical agent with profound and complex toxic effects. Traditionally, its toxic mechanism has been attributed to DNA alkylation-induced cytotoxicity and genomic instability. However, growing evidence indicates that dysregulation of epigenetic regulatory mechanisms constitutes a central link in SM toxicity, particularly in its long-term and delayed effects. Our study establishes an in vitro SM exposure model and employs integrated multi-omics profiling-including six histone modifications, DNA methylation, transcriptomic, and non-coding RNA analyses-to s
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive multi-omics characterization of the epigenetic changes induced by sulfur mustard exposure in human keratinocytes, revealing coordinated alterations in histone modifications, DNA methylation, and non-coding RNAs that may underlie its long-term toxic effects. The findings highlight epigenetic dysregulation as a central mechanism of SM toxicity beyond direct DNA damage.

papers.title: OMIDIENT: Multiomics Integration for Cancer by Dirichlet Auto-Encoder Networks.
papers.abstract: To achieve a more comprehensive understanding of cancer, novel computational methods are required for the integrative analysis of data from different molecular layers, such as genomics, transcriptomics, and epigenomics. Here, we present an innovative multi-omics integrative method that performs unsupervised representation learning, referred to as OMIDIENT: multiOMics Integration for cancer by DIrichlet auto-ENcoder neTworks. OMIDIENT provides a natural framework for modeling sparse and compositional latent representations by employing a deep generative model, where the latent space is distribu
papers.summary: OMIDIENT is a new computational method that integrates multiple types of cancer omics data (e.g., genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics) using a Dirichlet auto-encoder network. It performs unsupervised representation learning to produce sparse, compositional latent representations, offering a natural framework for modeling multi-omics data and potentially improving cancer subtype discovery and patient stratification.

papers.title: Somatic mobility of transposons is explosive and shaped by distinct integration biases in Arabidopsis thaliana.
papers.abstract: The movement of transposable elements (TEs) in somatic cells generates genetic and phenotypic diversity across the soma of individual organisms. This process is especially important in plants that display a sessile lifestyle, can regenerate from somatic cells, and continuously establish their germline from somatic stem cells. Yet, the scale and integration biases by which TEs may shape the plant soma remain unknown.
papers.summary: This study reveals that transposable element (TE) movement in somatic cells of Arabidopsis thaliana is far more extensive than previously appreciated, generating substantial genetic diversity within individual plants. The authors identify distinct integration biases that shape where TEs insert in the genome, providing new insights into how somatic TE mobility can influence plant development and evolution.

papers.title: Functional Analysis of IL-6 Genetic Variants and Their Potential Role in Lipid Homeostasis and Inflammatory Regulation in Colombian Athletes.
papers.abstract: Obesity and metabolic dysregulation are closely associated with chronic low-grade inflammation, in which interleukin-6 (IL-6) plays a key regulatory role. Genetic variation in the IL-6 gene may influence inflammatory responses and metabolic homeostasis. To identify single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) in the IL-6 gene in a cohort of Colombian high-performance athletes and to evaluate their potential functional and structural consequences using bioinformatic prediction and protein-modeling approaches. A descriptive observational study was conducted in a cohort of 23 high-performance Colombian athl
papers.summary: This study analyzed IL-6 gene variants in Colombian high-performance athletes and used bioinformatic tools to predict their potential functional and structural impacts on lipid homeostasis and inflammatory regulation. The findings suggest that certain genetic variants may influence inflammatory responses and metabolic health, though the study is descriptive and based on a small cohort.

papers.title: Assessing the Clinical Relevance of BRCA1 RING Domain Variants of Uncertain Significance.
papers.abstract: The BRCA1 protein serves an essential function in maintaining genomic integrity, to the extent that up to 80% of women carrying a pathogenic BRCA1 variant develop breast cancer (BC). Most of these carriers would benefit from prophylactic care, but genetic screens that uncover variants of uncertain significance (VUSs) do not provide insight on disease risk or clinical decision-making. In accordance with guidelines established by The American College of Molecular Genetics (ACMG) and Association for Molecular Pathology (AMP), this study produced computational and functional evidence to inform the
papers.summary: This study evaluates BRCA1 RING domain variants of uncertain significance (VUSs) using computational and functional evidence to clarify their clinical relevance. The findings help reclassify these variants, potentially improving risk assessment and clinical decision-making for carriers.

papers.title: AI-Guided DNA-Free and Genotype-Independent Genome Editing for Soybean Improvement.
papers.abstract: Soybean is a strategic crop for global protein and vegetable oil supply chains; however, genetic improvement remains constrained by genotype-dependent regeneration, variable transformation efficiency, and regulatory concerns regarding stable transgene integration. This review synthesizes emerging DNA-free and genotype-independent genome-editing frameworks for soybean, where genotype independence is defined as the ability to recover fertile, non-chimeric edited plants across elite germplasm. We critically examine the soybean genome-editing toolbox, including CRISPR-Cas9, Cas12a, multiplex editi
papers.summary: This review discusses emerging DNA-free and genotype-independent genome-editing strategies for soybean, aiming to overcome limitations in regeneration and transformation that hinder genetic improvement. It covers tools like CRISPR-Cas9 and Cas12a, with a focus on achieving fertile, non-chimeric edited plants across elite germplasm.

papers.title: MPOInt: An Epigenetics-Driven Workflow for Integrative Multi-Level Proteomics.
papers.abstract: Proteomics provides key insights into systems regulating cell behavior and can elucidate key epigenetic states influencing biological functions in health and disease. Integrating different modalities of proteomics (total, phospho, epi) allows for a comprehensive understanding of how systems change in response to a stimulus. A current limitation is that these data are often captured individually with a limited scope of how systems regulating biological processes interact. Integrative analyses are essential to accurately depict biological states but often require custom, time-consuming bioinform
papers.summary: MPOInt is a new computational workflow that integrates total, phospho, and epigenetic proteomics data to provide a more comprehensive view of cellular regulation. It addresses the limitation of analyzing these data types separately by offering a streamlined, integrative approach that can reveal how epigenetic states and signaling systems interact in health and disease.

papers.title: DNA methylation clock in bull sperm cells reveals the epigenetic aging characteristics and impact on fertility.
papers.abstract: Aging is a crucial factor influencing semen quality and fertility in bulls, with potential implications for reproductive management and genetic improvement programs. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying sperm cell aging is essential for assessing reproductive potential and improving livestock productivity.
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study develops a DNA methylation clock for bull sperm cells, revealing epigenetic aging characteristics and their impact on fertility. The findings provide a molecular tool to assess reproductive potential and improve livestock breeding programs.

papers.title: Deciphering chromatin architecture and dynamics in Plasmodium falciparum using the nucDetective pipeline.
papers.abstract: High-resolution analysis of cellular chromatin structure is crucial for uncovering developmental and cell-type-specific regulatory networks. We developed the nucDetective pipeline to provide a comprehensive evaluation of chromatin organisation. This involves assessing nucleosome positioning, occupancy, fuzziness, and array regularity. The pipeline was benchmarked by analysing the chromatin structure of the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) during its erythrocytic development cycle. Pf is characterised by a unique chromatin landscape, exhibiting unstable nucleosomes and a geno
papers.summary: The authors developed nucDetective, a computational pipeline for high-resolution analysis of chromatin organization, including nucleosome positioning, occupancy, fuzziness, and array regularity. They benchmarked it on the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum, revealing its unique chromatin landscape with unstable nucleosomes during the erythrocytic cycle. This tool provides a comprehensive approach to studying chromatin architecture and dynamics in organisms with atypical chromatin features.

papers.title: Nuclear mechanotransduction: tools for mechanical perturbation and chromatin characterization.
papers.abstract: Mechanical cues, ranging from matrix mechanical properties to dynamic mechanical loading, can be transmitted via structural proteins and signaling molecules to the nucleus to reorganize nuclear architecture and modulate chromatin accessibility. This mechanical regulation plays an important role in tissue regeneration and disease development. To gain deeper insights into the mechanical regulation of chromatin organization, it is essential to develop technologies that can apply mechanical inputs and characterize the resulting changes in nuclear structure and chromatin organization. Here, we revi
papers.summary: This review covers the emerging field of nuclear mechanotransduction, focusing on how mechanical cues from the environment are transmitted to the nucleus to alter chromatin organization and gene expression. It highlights the importance of developing new tools to apply mechanical perturbations and characterize nuclear and chromatin changes, which are key to understanding tissue regeneration and disease.

papers.title: Epigenetic regulation of vertebrate limb development: from field specification to tissue morphogenesis.
papers.abstract: Vertebrate limb development provides an excellent model for understanding how epigenetic mechanisms coordinate the integration of positional information and temporal signals to generate complex three-dimensional structures. An increasing body of evidence shows that chromatin-based mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and higher-order chromatin organization, define the competence of progenitor cells to respond to morphogenetic signals with spatial and temporal precision during limb development. This review explores how epigenetic mechanisms orchestrate and regulate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on how epigenetic mechanisms—including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and chromatin organization—coordinate vertebrate limb development by controlling progenitor cell competence and responses to morphogenetic signals. It highlights the role of chromatin-based regulation in integrating positional and temporal cues to generate complex limb structures.

papers.title: Whole genome dataset of bacterial strains isolated from urine analysed by Oxford Nanopore sequencing technologies in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
papers.abstract: A collection of 21 bacterial isolates recovered from urine specimens collected between September 2018 and February 2019 at Saint-Camille and SCHIPHRA hospitals in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, is presented. Isolates were identified using the API 20E system and tested for antibiotic susceptibility according to CASFM 2018 guidelines. Genomic DNA was extracted, barcoded with the SQK-RBK114.96 Rapid Barcoding Kit, and sequenced on an Oxford Nanopore MinION Mk1C using an R10.4.1 flowcell. Basecalling was performed with Dorado, and reads were quality filtered prior to de novo assembly with Flye, follow
papers.summary: This dataset provides whole-genome sequences of 21 bacterial isolates from urine samples collected in Burkina Faso, generated using Oxford Nanopore sequencing. It includes species identification and antibiotic susceptibility data, offering a resource for studying uropathogens in West Africa.

papers.title: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis of pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort: an exploratory study.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation profiling is a central tool for molecular classification of pediatric medulloblastoma. However, most reference datasets are derived from high-income countries, and the performance of established epigenetic markers in underrepresented populations remains insufficiently explored.
papers.journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
papers.summary: This study performs genome-wide DNA methylation analysis on pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort, an underrepresented population, to evaluate whether established epigenetic markers and molecular classification schemes perform reliably outside high-income country reference datasets. The findings provide an exploratory assessment of methylation patterns in this population, highlighting potential differences or confirmations of existing classification frameworks.

papers.title: Whole genome sequencing and molecular characterization of two Bacillus licheniformis strains isolated from hot springs in yellowstone ational park.
papers.abstract: Bacillus licheniformis is a Gram-positive, endospore-forming bacterium with broad biotechnological applications. Thermophilic environments such as hot springs may harbor strains with unique biosynthetic capabilities relevant to drug discovery. In this study, we isolated two B. licheniformis strains (S3 and S4) from the Five Sisters hot spring in Yellowstone National Park (68 °C and 65 °C, pH 8) and performed whole-genome sequencing using both the Oxford Nanopore long read and Illumina platforms. Hybrid de novo assembly using Unicycler yielded genome sizes of 4.80 Mbp (S3, 14 contigs) and 4.79
papers.summary: This study sequenced and characterized two Bacillus licheniformis strains isolated from hot springs in Yellowstone National Park using a hybrid approach combining Oxford Nanopore and Illumina sequencing. The genomes were assembled and analyzed to reveal biosynthetic gene clusters and other features relevant to drug discovery and biotechnology.

papers.title: Whole exome sequencing identified a novel compound heterozygous mutation of nephrocystin 4 in a child with nephronophthisis-a rare case report.
papers.abstract: Nephronophthisis (NPHP), an autosomal recessive kidney disorder characterized by chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis, is the most prevalent monogenic cause of end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Previous studies have identified variants in more than 20 genes, designated NPHP1 to NPHP20, and in additional loci as the genetic causes of NPHP. Here, a Chinese patient who presented with NPHP and proteinuria was enrolled. By employing whole exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing, we identified a rare compound heterozygous mutation in the NPHP4 gene (c.2611C > T/p.R871X and c.2768G > A/p.R923H) in the p
papers.summary: This case report identifies a novel compound heterozygous mutation in the NPHP4 gene (c.2611C>T/p.R871X and c.2768G>A/p.R923H) in a Chinese child with nephronophthisis and proteinuria, using whole exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing. The finding expands the mutation spectrum of NPHP4 and highlights the utility of whole exome sequencing for diagnosing rare genetic kidney diseases.

papers.title: Expanding genomic resources for heritage science: characterization of selected microbial isolates from salt-weathered historic sites.
papers.abstract: On historic masonry and plaster, moisture-driven salt crystallization cycles impose mechanical stress and create niches for halophilic and halotolerant microbial communities. Halotolerant/halophilic microorganisms isolated from these man-made heritage environments are usually not as well characterized as those isolated from natural environments and represent a genetic and biotechnological potential that has not been thoroughly studied to date.
papers.summary: This study expands genomic resources for heritage science by characterizing microbial isolates from salt-weathered historic sites, focusing on halophilic and halotolerant microorganisms. These microbes, often understudied compared to those from natural environments, represent untapped genetic and biotechnological potential.

papers.title: Integrative serum metabolite prioritization and functional screening identify N-acetyl-L-glutamine as a protective candidate in premature ovarian insufficiency.
papers.abstract: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a major cause of female infertility and is increasingly associated with systemic metabolic dysregulation. However, whether circulating metabolic alterations contribute causally to POI development or primarily arise as secondary consequences of ovarian failure remains unclear. In this study, bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), cell-based screening, and exploratory target-prioritization analyses were integrated to identify POI-related metabolites and functionally relevant candidates.
papers.summary: This study integrates bidirectional Mendelian randomization, cell-based screening, and target prioritization to identify circulating metabolites causally linked to premature ovarian insufficiency (POI). The authors find that N-acetyl-L-glutamine may be a protective metabolite against POI, suggesting a potential causal role for metabolic alterations in the disease.

papers.title: Epigenomics-Guided Multi-Omics Integration Uncovers a Lipid-Metabolic Signature with Translational Utility in Bladder Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Bladder cancer (BLCA) exhibits marked heterogeneity, and current classifiers provide limited guidance for prognosis or treatment. Because epigenetic reprogramming and metabolic rewiring jointly shape BLCA biology, we sought to identify epigenomically informed biomarkers with functional relevance. Methods: Epigenome (genome-wide promoter DNA methylation) and matched transcriptome (RNA sequencing) profiles from tumor and adjacent normal samples were integrated to identify genes with concordant differential methylation and expression patterns. A survival-oriented machine learning fram
papers.summary: This study integrates epigenomic and transcriptomic data from bladder cancer tumors to identify genes with coordinated methylation and expression changes, then uses machine learning to derive a lipid-metabolic gene signature with prognostic and potentially therapeutic utility. The signature offers a new biomarker approach that reflects the interplay between epigenetic reprogramming and metabolic rewiring in bladder cancer.

papers.title: Dorsal Root Ganglion as a Hub for Peripheral Sensitization: A Hierarchical Regulation Model and Translational Progress.
papers.abstract: The high attrition rate of analgesic candidates in clinical trials stems largely from a reductionist reliance on rodent models and a neglect of the spatiotemporal complexity of nociception. Positioning the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) as the core computational hub for peripheral sensitization, this review proposes a "Hierarchical Regulation Model" to integrate fragmented mechanisms into a systemic framework. We stratify peripheral sensitization into three interlocking tiers: an acute tier driven by ion channel functional remodeling (eg, Nav1.7/1.8, Transient Receptor Potential (TRP) family); an
papers.summary: This review proposes a 'Hierarchical Regulation Model' that positions the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) as a central computational hub for peripheral sensitization, integrating ion channel remodeling, transcriptional changes, and other mechanisms into a three-tier framework. It aims to address the high attrition rate of analgesic candidates by providing a more systemic understanding of nociception beyond traditional rodent models.
